To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most effective exploration strategies are the ones based on uncertainty estimates, that the most effective way of estimating the uncertainty is by means of the upper confidence bound, and that exploration strategies should be adapted to the environment.

the following exploration strategies are effective: - Epsilon-greedy - UCB1 - Thompson Sampling - Optimistic initialization - Optimistic action value estimates - Optimistic state value estimates - Optimism in the face of uncertainty - Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) - Upper Confidence Bound for Trees (UCT) - Upper Confidence for Trees with Bandit Sampling (UCTBS)

(i) the best exploration strategies are those that are based on the information gained so far; (ii) the best exploration strategy is the one that is tailored for the problem being solved; (iii) there are many ways to define an effective exploration strategy, and it depends on the problem being solved which one is the best; and (iv) exploration is a fundamental issue in reinforcement and it is still an open problem.
